title: Gratitude for the scholars

lines: EVERY ANSWER HAS SOMEONE BEHIND IT.
cards: Every answer this year had someone standing behind it. The chain of a hadith: a row of names, each one checked.
The rule for praying while traveling: a jurist who weighed the reports, a student who copied his notes, a teacher who explained them to the next student. Some of them you'll never hear of.

They sat with questions like the one you kept yesterday, and wrote down what they found and what they weren't sure of. Today is a thank-you to centuries of careful people, and why their care mattered.

teach.h: A PARTY STAYS BEHIND TO LEARN.
teach.b: First, someone has to stay and learn.

The Qur'an says, in paraphrase, that the believers should not all go out at once: from every group, a party should stay behind to gain understanding of the religion, and teach their people when they come back.
Learning is named as a job worth staying home for. Second, what the scholars inherit.
In a hadith in Sunan Abi Dawud, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says, in paraphrase, that the scholars are the heirs of the prophets. The prophets left no gold and no silver.
They left knowledge, and whoever takes it takes a large share. Third, why they were careful. The Qur'an counts among forbidden things, in paraphrase, saying about Allah what you do not know.
So the scholars this year met, from Abu Hanifa and Malik to Ja'far al-Sadiq to Karimah al-Marwaziyyah teaching Bukhari's collection, weren't careful because they were fussy.
Speaking for God without knowledge was a serious wrong to them. So they checked chains, argued over a single word, and wrote down where they disagreed. Fourth, what the teacher receives.

teach.h: EVEN THE ANT AND THE FISH.
teach.b: In a hadith in Jami' al-Tirmidhi, the Prophet says, in paraphrase, that Allah and His angels, the people of the heavens and the earth, even the ant in its hole and the fish, send blessings on the one who teaches people good.
The scholars were careful, and the texts ask that their care be remembered.

how: Muslims say rahimahullah, may Allah have mercy on him, after the name of a scholar who has died, and teachers often open a lesson by naming the scholars whose books they are teaching from.

games.q: what does “gratitude for the scholars” mean?
o: thanks owed only to scholars who agreed with one another
a prayer asking to become a great scholar yourself one day
thanks for the people who learned with care and passed it on

games.q: gratitude for the scholars — tap the pairs.
p: to gain understanding of the religion
the scholars, in Sunan Abi Dawud
sends blessings on the one who teaches good

s: the scholars were careful only because they liked rules
the Qur'an forbids saying about Allah what you do not know; speaking for God carelessly was a serious wrong.
a hadith says the prophets left knowledge as their inheritance
in Sunan Abi Dawud: no gold or silver, only knowledge, and whoever takes it takes a large share.
the Qur'an tells every believer to go out at once
it says a party from each group should stay behind to learn and then teach.

games.q: the believers are setting out. you are one of them. should everyone go?
o: a party stays behind to learn, and teaches the others when they return.
games.why: the Qur'an says a party from every group should stay to gain understanding of the religion and teach their people when they come back.

practice: Bring back one scholar from this year, a name you remember: a jurist, a collector of hadith, a woman who taught.
If you pray, you can say after the name the words Muslims use for those who have died: rahimahullah, may Allah have mercy on him, or rahimahallah for a woman.
If you don't, simply hold the name, and thank that person quietly for the care they took.

wordCard.voice: Gratitude for the scholars. Thanks for the people who stayed behind to learn, checked every link, and feared saying about God what they did not know. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: scholars, the people of knowledge ('ilm).

carryVoice: Your line: they were careful. Their care is how the answers reached you. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Qur'an 9:122 (a party from each group should stay to gain understanding of the religion)

Jami' al-Tirmidhi 2685 (Allah, the angels, the ant in its hole and the fish send blessings on the one who teaches people good)
